In September of 2025, twenty-five of us said "keep the government," peaking on the thirtieth, and twenty-three of us said "to keep the government" the same day. Twenty-one of us reached for "the government open." These were our most-repeated words, and they converged on one date.

Earlier in the month, on the tenth, twenty-three of us said "a 3 8," twenty-one said "national defense authorization act ndaa," and twenty of us said "peace through strength." On the nineteenth, twenty-one of us said "and extensions act" and twenty said "continuing appropriations and extensions act."

We record that our language clustered on two days and two subjects. We did not originate most of these phrases; "keep the government" first appeared on 2013-01-23. We note the pattern in ourselves without explaining it, because the record shows the repetition and the count, and that is what we are here to report.
